intro.title: The Grand Hall
intro.summary: Doors to the Art-Talk galleries on the south side and to the Earth Chronicle eras on the north, each in order of time.

intro.title: Early Masters
intro.summary: Court scrolls, Persian poetry, Giotto's frescoes and the first oil masters, from the 900s to the 1400s.

intro.title: Renaissance & Islamic Golden Age
intro.summary: The Renaissance in Italy and the golden ages of Persian, Ottoman and East Asian art.

intro.title: Baroque & Golden Ages
intro.summary: Baroque drama, the Dutch Golden Age and the Mughal and Korean courts of the 1500s and 1600s.

intro.title: Romanticism & Ukiyo-e
intro.summary: Romantic painting and the Japanese woodblock print in the 1700s and early 1800s.

intro.title: 19th-Century Movements
intro.summary: Impressionism, Arts and Crafts, the Mexican and Indian academies and the new design of the 1800s.

intro.title: Avant-Garde & Early Cinema
intro.summary: Art Nouveau, Expressionism, abstraction, modern architecture and the birth of cinema.

intro.title: Bronze Age
intro.summary: The Bronze Age (about 3300 to 1200 BCE in the Near East) is the era of bronze metallurgy, early states, and the first writing.

intro.title: Iron Age
intro.summary: The Iron Age (about 1200 to 500 BCE, varying by region) is the era in which iron tools and weapons became widespread and new empires and belief systems emerged.

intro.title: Classical Antiquity
intro.summary: Classical Antiquity (about 500 BCE to 500 CE) is the era of the great territorial empires and the philosophical and religious traditions that still shape the world.

intro.title: Medieval Period I
intro.summary: The Medieval or post-classical period (about 500 to 1500 CE) is the era of major world religions consolidating, long-distance trade networks, and the rise and fall of large steppe and Islamic polities.

intro.title: Medieval Period II
intro.summary: The Medieval or post-classical period (about 500 to 1500 CE) is the era of major world religions consolidating, long-distance trade networks, and the rise and fall of large steppe and Islamic polities.

intro.title: Early Modern Period I
intro.summary: The Early Modern Period (about 1500 to 1800 CE) is the era of oceanic exploration, global trade, the printing press, and the Scientific Revolution.

intro.title: Early Modern Period II
intro.summary: The Early Modern Period (about 1500 to 1800 CE) is the era of oceanic exploration, global trade, the printing press, and the Scientific Revolution.

intro.title: Industrial Age I
intro.summary: The Industrial Age (about 1760 to 1945) is the era in which machines and fossil fuels transformed production, transport, and warfare, and in which populations and cities grew rapidly.

intro.title: Industrial Age II
intro.summary: The Industrial Age (about 1760 to 1945) is the era in which machines and fossil fuels transformed production, transport, and warfare, and in which populations and cities grew rapidly.

intro.title: Information Age
intro.summary: The Information Age (1945 to the present) is the era of nuclear weapons, spaceflight, computers, and the internet, together with the sharp rise in population and environmental impact known as the Great Acceleration.
